record.paper_title: A New Paradigm for Scattering Theory of Linear and Nonlinear Waves: Review and Open Problems
record.original_question: For a short-lived perturbation W(x,t) added to a stationary potential V0(x), with V(x,t) = V0(x) + W(x,t) and W(x,t) = 0 for |t| > 1, can the scattering matrix determine the time-dependent perturbation W?

evidence.quote: Problem 2 Short-Lived Potential Suppose first that the target is an object centered at the origin, which at time zero start moving to the point (1,1,1) and then come back after a finite time and is at rest forever. This is an example of a short lived potential. So, the general question is, given a potential of the form V (x,t ) = V0(x) +W (x,t ), W = 0 for |t|> 1.
Can the scattering matrix determine W ? See Kian (2017).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Schrödinger equation on $\mathbb{R}^n$ (with $n\ge 2$)
\[
 i\partial_t u(x,t) = -\Delta u(x,t) + V(x,t)\, u(x,t), \qquad (x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R},
\]
where the potential has the form
\[
 V(x,t) = V_0(x) + W(x,t),
\]
with $V_0:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ a fixed stationary short-range potential and $W:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ a bounded compactly supported perturbation satisfying
\[
 W(x,t) = 0 \quad\text{for all } |t|>1.
\]
For such $V$, the wave operators $\Omega_\pm = \mathrm{s\text{-}lim}_{t\to\pm\infty} U(0,t) e^{-it(-\Delta)}$ exist (where $U(t,s)$ is the propagator of the time-dependent Hamiltonian $-\Delta+V(\cdot,t)$), and the scattering operator is defined by $S = \Omega_+^*\Omega_-$.

Question: Assuming $V_0$ is known, does knowledge of the scattering operator $S$ uniquely determine the time-dependent perturbation $W(x,t)$? Equivalently, if $W_1$ and $W_2$ are two such short-lived perturbations giving rise to the same scattering operator (with the same background $V_0$), must $W_1 \equiv W_2$?
artifact.status_search_result: Web search did not yield a definitive resolution. Related uniqueness results exist for inverse scattering with time-dependent potentials (e.g., Stefanov; Kian's work on recovery of time-dependent coefficients in wave equations), and a 2025 paper on backscattering for time-dependent potentials appears, but no clear evidence was found that the specific short-lived-perturbation problem above has been settled in full generality.

status_evidence.title: The Backscattering Problem for Time-Dependent Potentials
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) work on inverse backscattering for time-dependent potentials, indicating the area remains active.
status_evidence.claim: Time-dependent inverse scattering uniqueness questions are still being investigated.

status_evidence.title: Uniqueness of the multi-dimensional inverse scattering problem for time-dependent potentials
status_evidence.snippet: Classical uniqueness results for inverse scattering with time-dependent potentials.
status_evidence.claim: Some uniqueness results exist for related time-dependent inverse scattering problems.
